# science

<!-- ops:identity start — generated by ops-docs; edit identity.toml -->
*The daily surface of verifiably: the layer people and agents use*

The commands a researcher or a coding agent runs in place of a folder of scripts and result tables: state a question as a typed claim, hold the data, declare the analysis, run it sealed, verify it from scratch, and read what the checked results add up to. Its scientific records live in a beliefs corpus, checked by the kernel, so the work stays traceable whoever did it. A CLI and an MCP server.

Authority: `docs/specs/2026-08-31-command-framework-design.md`

## Install

From a checkout, with `beliefs` checked out beside it as an editable path dependency:

```sh
cd python && uv sync
```

## Usage

`science` is the CLI (`uv run science <command>` under `python/`); `science mcp serve`
serves the same commands over MCP on stdio.

A session follows one question from its data to a belief, where an ad hoc project would
leave a folder of scripts and result tables that nobody can trace back: `dataset` copies
the data into the store and fingerprints it by its hash, so every later step can prove
which bytes it used; `claim` records the question as a typed claim; `spec` freezes the
analysis before it runs; `run` executes it once in a sandbox that sees only the captured
code, software and data, with no network; `assess` reads the verdict its outputs
support; `verify` replays the run and compares; `belief` evaluates what the checked,
independent assessments add up to; and `next` ranks which claims are ready to work on.
Every write on that path is a corpus record and every read names the records it used,
so the chain from a conclusion back to its data survives the session and reads the same
whether a person or an agent did the work. The
[mm30 record](docs/records/2026-09-23-mm30-through-the-commands.md) is one real
analysis through exactly that path. The command surface, from `tools/cli.toml`:

- The belief path: `dataset`, `claim`, `spec`, `run`, `assess`, `verify`, `belief`,
  `next`.
- Coordination: `project`, `question`, `hypothesis`, `task`, `decide`, `revise`,
  `reuse`, `project-select`, `projects`, `project-show`.
- Sharing, between worlds (the [commons design](docs/specs/2026-09-30-science-commons-design.md)):
  `publish`, `publish-preview`, `provider-inspect`, `provider-bind`, `adopt`, `fetch`,
  `show`.
- The world: `status`, `build`, `epoch`, `serve`, `mcp`, `adapters`.

Every command that opens the world (all but `build` and `adapters`) reads one
configuration file, named by `--config` or the `SCIENCE_CONFIG` environment variable,
and refuses when neither is given; nothing is discovered from the working directory. The file names the world, its corpus roots, the operations and store
roots and the activated domains: §9.1 of the
[command framework design](docs/specs/2026-08-31-command-framework-design.md) lists its
keys, and §3.1 of the [mm30 record](docs/records/2026-09-23-mm30-through-the-commands.md)
creates a world and writes one. An entry of `contracts` or `read_contracts` is a contract
document's path, or for a successor contract a table
`{ document = "<path>", predecessors = ["<oldest>", …] }` naming its lineage. With that file,

```sh
uv run science status --config <path to science.toml>
```

prints the world: corpora and their lifecycle status, the current epoch, and record
counts by kind. Corpus writes run as kernel acts through an attended `beliefs` session,
permit-checked per act and deduplicated through its ledger. Two classes of write leave
no corpus record: `project-select` records the session's selection as a line in that
session ledger, and `provider-bind` and `adopt` record sharing lines there. Science keeps
the sharing registry under the configured `sharing_root`:
its pins and provider bindings are a projection of those sharing lines, written after
each line and rebuilt from them, beside the adopted corpora the kernel restores there.
Science also keeps presentation-only historical sharing-report tails under
`operations_root/tails/<session_id>/<invocation_id>.json`. These sidecars hold commentary,
separate from kernel evidence and close outcomes; they are not recomputed from current
state. Reports rebuild every pin block from the ledger and append the saved tail.
An absent sidecar means an empty tail; losing a nonempty tail loses that commentary and
stales its cursor, while every effect stays recoverable. Exact historical replay needs
the sidecar retained beside the ledger.

`publish-preview` and new `publish` attempts use the same Own classification as
belief acceptance: configured markerless roots, including restored replicas, are
declared as this installation's own. Sharing-registry roots remain excluded even
when hand-listed, and marker-bearing roots retain publication attribution. Both
commands read every configured mount, refuse duplicate claimed carriers, and
require exactly one write mount; input-read errors propagate. Resume uses the
attempt's frozen selection and attributions without reclassifying ownership.

## Layout

- `commands/` — one directory per command: its declaration and prompt.
- `adapters/` — the generated harness adapters (Claude Code).
- `python/` — the package: the dispatcher, the CLI and MCP surfaces, the writer service.
- `docs/specs/`, `docs/plans/`, `docs/records/` — designs, plans and records.
